title: Concept: Two-argument open in perl — review required
description: In perl, open is called in its two-argument form. Perl parses the second argument for a leading mode character, so "|cmd" executes a command and ">file" writes. This behaviour is documented but easy to forget when the filename is a variable that previously only held paths.
applicability: perl scripts that open files named by input or configuration.
risk: Command execution or file truncation through a crafted name; MEDIUM severity.
